Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for last week's demo. Our legal/privacy team has a short DPIA template they run with new vendors for risk classification before procurement. I've attached the template (PDF) and a short list of questions. Can you confirm who at Redwood will complete it and share a target date?

High-level asks:
- Overview of what personal data Redwood processes on behalf of NovoHealth (including diagnostics metadata)
- Data flow (where stored / regions) and subprocessors
- Retention and deletion controls for patient-identifiable tokens
- Any automated decision-making / risk mitigations

We'd like the completed DPIA and a one-page summary by EOD Thursday 05/07 if possible.

Thanks,
Amelia

Subject: Re: DPIA template submission — Redwood responses (draft)

Hi team — attached is a draft DPIA response and a simple data flow diagram. I pulled together legal responses to the questions in the Novo template and added notes where we should confirm implementation details (marked TODO). Neha, please review the technical sections and confirm the storage regions and retention windows.

Key points I included in draft:
- Data controller/processor stance: Redwood will typically be a processor for hosted customers; for Dedicated/Private deployments the role may vary (noted in Q2).
- Categories of data: we described user-generated content, request metadata, and optional PII fields (names/emails) — we flagged diagnostics metadata as covered under request metadata and subject to customer-configured retention.
- Subprocessors: listed major cloud providers + logging/observability vendors; included our subprocessors page link.
- Data transfers: SCCs are used for transfers from EU customers; we provided a link to our SCC summary doc.
- Automated decisioning: we marked N/A for any automated decision-making on patient outcomes; clarified model outputs are probabilistic and subject to customer interpretation.
- Risk mitigations: encryption in transit/at rest, access controls, logging/audit, and DPIA follow-up commitments.

I've attached: Redwood_DPIA_Response_v1.pdf (redlineable), redwood_data_flow_diagram.png, SCCs-summary.txt.

Neha — can you confirm the following by EOD today:
1) Storage regions for NovoHealth (they asked specifically about where patient-related tokens could be stored)
2) Retention default for KV cache and prompt logs and whether we can offer shorter retention for this account
3) Any HIPAA-specific caveats we should add if Novo requests a Business Associate Agreement (BAA)

If all looks good I'll finalize and send to Amelia with the one-page exec summary.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPIA_Response_v1.pdf; redwood_data_flow_diagram.png; SCCs-summary.txt

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Amelia Grant <amelia.grant@novohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2026 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPIA template submission — tech confirmations

Laura / Karthik / Amelia,

Thanks — reviewed the draft and confirmed the technical items below. I'm attaching the updated response PDF with the technical answers filled and the data flow diagram updated to call out region-level storage and the optional customer-configured retention windows.

Technical confirmations:
- Storage regions: For NovoHealth (requested US-only), we can pin hosting to us-west-2 or us-east-1 depending on capacity. By default hosted customers have region affinity; Dedicated/Private can be placed in customer VPC.
- Patient-identifiable tokens: not stored persistently by default in our hosted flow; tokens are kept in encrypted KV cache for up to 24 hours by default and scrubbed per customer's retention policy. We can offer a 0-day token persistence option (evict immediately) for regulated accounts under a contract addendum.
- Retention: Prompt logs and model context are retained 30 days by default for hosted customers; we can reduce retention to 7 or 0 days for enterprise agreements.
- HIPAA: Redwood is willing to negotiate a BAA for customers with covered data. Technical safeguards documented; legal/ops must sign BAA and validate operational controls.

Next steps for submission:
- Laura: incorporate these technical confirmations into the final DPIA (I've attached updated PDF).
- Karthik: I'll stand by to support any follow-up clarifications with Novo's privacy team.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPIA_Response_v1_neha_edits.pdf; redwood_data_flow_diagram.png
